replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the route deviation is established, and the rider is refunded SGD 10.75 of the SGD 26.04 charged.

Finding on the route. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00106), which records 10.78 km driven between the recorded pickup at Blk 79 Toa Payoh Central and the dropoff at Bugis Junction, against a booked optimal of 7.2 km (EV-TRIP-00106). The excess is 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. That clears both establishment tests in POL-RD-01 (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so a deviation exists. The trip record's rounded 10.8 km is a convenience copy and may not be used for the threshold test; on the trace figure the excess stops just short of the 50% materiality line, so this is NOT a MATERIAL deviation. It is also just short of the 8.0 km absolute alternative. The consequence is that POL-RD-06 is not engaged, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no driver-conduct referral follows; in any event the driver's profile shows no pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 across 96 completed_trips_90d), so the result would be the same had the check been run.

No exoneration. There is no traffic advisory in the record: EV-ADVIS-00106-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no closure can be asserted and POL-RD-03 cannot apply. The single chat message (EV-CHAT-00106) is the rider's own question at 08:46:30, not an instruction given before the vehicle left the corridor; it carries waypoint_hint null and names no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause exonerates nothing. The pickup and dropoff were never amended (all amendment fields null), so POL-RD-05 does not apply, and the vehicle was a metered taxi, not a pooled ride, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not displace it. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 10 s sampling, max gap 0.0 s, no 500 m jumps), so no independent corroboration is required and no escalation is triggered.

The refund, line by line. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19.0) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32. Refund = charged_total 26.04 - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.75. The 5.50 of CTE ERP (Braddell Rd 3.00, Chin Swee tunnel 2.50, both on_optimal_route false) is already comprehended inside this figure, because the recomputation credits only gantries on the optimal route and the optimal route carries none; it is itemised for transparency and is deliberately not added on top, so the rider recovers 10.75 and not 16.25. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis and well under 90% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

To the rider: you are refunded SGD 10.75, not the full SGD 26.04 you pleaded. The recomputed fare of SGD 15.32 is a genuine fare for a 7.2 km, 19-minute trip, so there is no basis to return the whole amount. To the driver: the correction is limited to the excess distance attributable to the route taken; the deviation is not material, no pattern was found on your profile, and no referral or penalty attaches to this trip beyond that fare correction.
